In, Alverson, K.D., et al., eds. Paleoclimate, Global Change and the Future, IGBP Series PAGES, Springer-Verlag: New York

description: Services that allow a user to interact with a Gazetteer service.
name: GAZETTEER APPLICATION SERVICES

description: Determining the origin of a biological pollutant, typically fecal matter, using unique microbiological, genotypic, phenotypic, and chemical patterns and comparing the patterns to different source locations.
name: MICROBIAL SOURCE TRACKING

description: Phylum Chordata. Class Actinopterygii. Salmon, a common name for ray-finned fish, are a commercially important anadromous fish. Trout, common name for freshwater fish, have fins without spine and small adipose fin near the tail.
name: SALMONS/TROUTS

description: Phylum Chordata. Class Mammalia. Order Carnivora. Otters, Family Mustelidae, are small carnivorous mammals with short legs, round ears, tail tappering to a point, nose with a blunt tip, and guard hair covering insulating coarse fur.
name: OTTERS

description: Marks the locations where said glaciers become anchored on bedrock (i.e., the estimated coastline underneath the ice).
name: GROUNDING LINE
reference: National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC)

description: The minimum or maximum length of the ice or ice edge into the open water. Also refers to the extent of the ice pack into the open ocean (which varies seasonally).
name: ICE EXTENT

description: Drought is a protracted period of deficient precipitation resulting in extensive damage to crops, resulting in loss of yield. Lack of rainfall for an extended period of time can bring farmers and major metropolitan areas to their knees. It does not take very long; a few rain-free weeks spreads panic and shrivels crops. A drought forecast would be issued for one of the following: Meteorological - a measure of departure of precipitation from normal. Due to climatic differences what is considered a drought in one location may not be a drought in another location. Agricultural - refers to a situation when the amount of moisture in the soil no longer meets the needs of a particular crop and can also affect livestock and other dry-land agricultural operations. Hydrological - occurs when surface and subsurface water supplies are below normal. Socioeconomic - refers to the situation that occurs when physical water shortage begins to affect people.
name: DROUGHT FORECAST

description: An area of land where precipitation collects and drains off into a common outlet, such as into a river, bay, or other body of water, but considers the flow of ice over the frozen continent.
name: BASINS
reference: National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC)

description: A measure of the average kinetic energy of the vibration of water molecules.
name: WATER TEMPERATURE
reference: Water Resources Glossaries from the USGS

description: Radiation with wavelengths roughly between 200 and 400 nanometers. These wavelengths are shorter than those which characterize visible light. Observations from satellites in the UV and extreme UV (EUV) wavelengths have demonstrated the sun's UV variability over short time scales of days and weeks. UV variability is linked to solar magnetic activity phenomena such as flares and plages. Studies of the UV and EUV irradiance variability may have indicated influences on the Earth's climate dynamics.
name: SOLAR ULTRAVIOLET EMISSIONS
reference: Foukal, P., ed. 1987. Solar Radiative Output Variation: Proceedings of a Workshop held Nov. 9-11, 1987 at NCAR, Boulder, CO. Cambridge Research and Instrumentation, Inc.

description: The identification, assessment, design, and manipulation of features or values of a landscape.
name: LANDSCAPE MANAGEMENT

description: A wave formed by transfer of wind energy into water.
name: WIND WAVES
reference: Garrison, T. 1993. Oceanography, an Invitation to Marine Science. Wadsworth Pubishing Co. p. 529.

description: Reports providing information on predicted climate trends.
name: CLIMATE ADVISORIES

description: Pertaining to an area between 15 and 35 degrees N & S characterized by less than 300 mm annual rainfall and consisting of vegetation adapted to hot, dry conditions.
name: DESERT SCRUB

description: Change in Tropical Storm position with respect to time.
name: TROPICAL STORM MOTION

description: The intrinsic color of the mineral.
name: COLOR

description: Total mass of a glacier.
name: GLACIER MASS

description: The exposure of the magnetic field. An electric field is produced by voltage, which is the pressure used to push the electrons through the wire, much like water being pushed through a pipe. As the voltage increases, the electric field increases in strength. A magnetic field results from the flow of current through wires or electrical devices and increases in strength as the current increases. These two fields together are referred to as electric and magnetic fields, or EMFs.
name: ELECTRIC/MAGNETIC FIELD EXPOSURE

description: Advisories providing reports of current volcanic ash plumes or dust clouds and the projected trajectory of the ash or dust.
name: DUST/ASH ADVISORIES

description: Any measure related to waste from animals including, but not limited to: manure, methane gas, by-products, nitrates, waste water, and others.
name: ANIMAL MANURE AND WASTE
reference: Adapted from: Herren, R.V., and R.L. Donahue. 1991. The Agriculture Dictionary, Delmar Publishers INC. Albany, New york. 553pp.

description: Retrieves client-specified subset of client-specified coverage (or image) dataset.
name: WEB COVERAGE SERVICE

description: Reports providing information pertaining to the study of frozen seawater over the ocean surface. Sea Ice Advisory Services include warnings for ice melting, and daily analyses through real time data and forecast.
name: SEA ICE

description: The related chemical and geological properties of the ocean.
name: MARINE GEOCHEMISTRY

description: Phylum Echinodermata. Class Echinoidea. Marine invertebrates with five-fold symmetry visible on the test and spines used for protection
name: SEA URCHINS

description: The (microwave) signal reflected by elements of an illuminated scene back in the direction of the radar. It is so named to make clear the difference between energy scattered in arbitrary directions, and that which returns to the radar and thus may be received and recorded by the sensor.
name: RADAR BACKSCATTER

description: Phylum Chordata. Class Aves. Order Charadriiformes. Sandpipers are shorebirds with long bodies and legs and narrow wings
name: SANDPIPERS

description: The upward motion of seawater anywhere in the oceans.
name: OCEAN UPWELLING/DOWNWELLING
reference: Oceanography: Perspectives on a Fluid Earth, Steve Neshyba, John Wiley & Sons, 1987.

description: A host (e.g., a human) with all of its associated symbiotic organisms (e.g., a human’s microbiome).
name: HOLOBIONT

description: Greenhouse gases, including carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapor, absorb and re-emit thermal infrared radiation, thereby regulating Earth’s temperature and climate. While they are essential for maintaining habitable conditions by preventing heat loss into space, excessive emissions from human activities amplify this effect, contributing to climate change.
name: GREENHOUSE GASES
reference: Stephen H. Schneider, The Greenhouse Effect: Science and Policy. Science 243, 771-781 (1989). DOI: 10.1126/science.243.4892.771

description: Categories defining the land in some way, such as by slope, land cover, and type
name: LAND USE CLASSES
reference: Remote Sensing and Image Interpretation, John Wiley & Sons, 1994.

description: A method of exploration geophysics that uses the principles of seismology to estimate of the properties of the Earth's subsurface from reflected seismic waves. This measurement is also known as seismic reflection.
name: REFLECTION
reference: Sheriff, R. E., Geldart, L. P., (1995), 2nd Edition. Exploration Seismology. Cambridge University Press

description: Estuaries form a transition zone between river environments and ocean environments and are subject to both marine influences, such as tides, waves, and the influx of saline water; and riverine influences, such as flows of fresh water and sediment. The inflow of both seawater and freshwater provide high levels of nutrients in both the water column and sediment, making estuaries among the most productive natural habitats in the world.
name: ESTUARIES

description: Bioinformatics, as related to genetics and genomics, is a scientific subdiscipline that involves using computer technology to collect, store, analyze, and disseminate biological data and information, such as DNA and amino acid sequences or annotations about those sequences. Scientists and clinicians use databases that organize and index such biological information to increase our understanding of health and disease and, in certain cases, as part of medical care.
name: BIOINFORMATICS

description: The East Atlantic Jet pattern is the third primary mode of low frequency variability found over the North Atlantic, appearing between April and August. This pattern also consists of a north-south dipole of anomaly centers, with one main center located over the high latitudes of the eastern North Atlantic ... and Scandinavia, and the other center located over Northern Africa and the Mediterranean Sea. A positive phase of the EA-Jet pattern reflects an intensification of westerlies over the central latitudes of the eastern North Atlantic and over much of Europe, while a negative phase reflects a strong split-flow configuration over these regions, sometimes in association with long-lived blocking anticyclones in the vicinity of Greenland and Great Britain.
name: EAST ATLANTIC JET PATTERN
reference: NOAA/ National Weather Service National Centers for Environmental Prediction Climate Prediction Center

description: Lacustrine Wetlands are lakes, or former lakes, that are naturally filled with shallow water at certain times and more or less drained at other times.
name: LACUSTRINE WETLANDS

description: Phylum Chordata. Class Mammalia. Order Carnivora. Family Mustelidae are small carnivorous mammals with short legs, round ears and thick fur.
name: MARTENS/WEASELS/WOLVERINES

description: A fabric or edifice that is constructed, such as a house, church, etc.
name: BUILDINGS

description: The merger or meeting of two or more objects (or subjects) that seem to inseparably bind their respective forces or attributes into a point of junction.
name: CONFLUENCE

description: Migration is a persistent movement across different habitats in response to seasonal changes in resource availability and quality. Migratory rates and routes are observed for many migrating species.
name: MIGRATORY RATES/ROUTES
reference: Feldhamer, G., L.Drickamer, S.Vessey, J.Merritt. 1999. Mammalogy: Adaptation, Diversity, Ecology. McGraw Hill-Hill Companies, Inc.

description: The ratio of the heat absorbed (or released) by a system to the corresponding temperature rise (or fall).
name: LAND HEAT CAPACITY
reference: Huschle, R.E., ed. 1959. Glossary of Meteorology, American Meteorological Society, Boston, MA.

description: Elements or compounds of gaseous form, dissolved in seawater. When keyed in a DIF, they do not typically include carbon dioxide, oxygen, nitrogen, or nitrous oxide, since these are their own variables.
name: DISSOLVED GASES

description: Atmospheric aerosol particles derived from biogenic or anthropogenic sulfur emissions; comprised of sulfate compounds (e.g., DMS, sulfuric acid, ammonium sulfate).
name: SULFATE PARTICLES

description: Active layer, also called frost zone or mollisol, is part of the soil included with the suprapermafrost layer (i.e., existing above permafrost) that usually freezes in winter and thaws in summer. Its bottom surface is the frost table, beneath which may lie permafrost or talik. The depth of the active layer varies anywhere from a few inches to several feet.
name: ACTIVE LAYER
reference: American Meteorological Society Glossary of Meteorology Online "http://amsglossary.allenpress.com/glossary"

description: Photosynthesis is the synthesis of carbohydrates from carbon dioxide and water by chlorphyll using light as energy with oxygen as a byproduct.
name: PHOTOSYNTHESIS
reference: Krebs, Charles K. Ecology - 4th ed. 1994. HarperCollins College Publishers, New York, New York.

description: Isotopes are a form of an element with a certain number of neutrons, for example carbon exists in three isotopes: C12, C13, and C14. Some isotopes are naturally unstable and spontaneously decay at a fixed rate; other isotopes are stable.
name: ISOTOPES

description: CH3Br, this halocarbon is released, to a degree, naturally from the oceans, but is more commonly released from its anthropogenic use as a soil fumigant or pesticide. Methyl bromide is persistent enough to reach the stratosphere where it photochemically decomposes to yield atomic bromine (radical) and proceeds to destroy stratospheric ozone in the same manner as the atomic chlorine radical. On an atom-for-atom basis, stratospheric bromine is more efficient at destroying ozone than is chlorine because the HBr reservoir species is more photochemically active than HCl; however, there is much less of hydrogen bromide in the stratosphere. Recent data suggest that since 1998 atmospheric concentrations have dropped 13% due the CH3Br use limitations mandated by the Montreal Protocol
name: METHYL BROMIDE
reference: [New York Times Aug. 16, 2003] [Baird, Colin. Environmental Chemistry. (1999) W.H. Freeman, New York.]

description: The quantity of plant materials resulting from cultivation or growth. Includes all comercial crops, as well as plant biomass yields (i.e. amount of grass produced per unit land in natural agroecosystems (e.g. rangeland)). Does not include PRODUCT yield (e.g. bushels of wheat vs. lbs. flour).
name: CROP/PLANT YIELDS
reference: Adapted from: Herren, R.V., and R.L. Donahue. 1991. The Agriculture Dictionary, Delmar Publishers INC. Albany, New york. 553pp.

description: The tendency for higher air temperatures to persist in urban areas as aresult of heat absorbed and emitted by buildings and asphalt, tending to make cities warmer than the surrounding countryside.
name: URBAN HEAT ISLAND

description: Digital reference services that use the Internet to connect people with people who can answer questions about the biological sciences.
name: ASK-A BIOLOGIST

description: A widespread convectively induced straight-line windstorm. Specifically, the term is defined as any family of downburst clusters produced by an extratropical mesoscale convective system. Derechos may or may not be accompanied by tornadoes. Such events were first recognized in the Corn Belt region of the United States, but have since been observed in many other areas of the midlatitudes.
name: DERECHO
reference: Glossary of Meteorology, American Meteorological Society, 2016. Johns, R. H., and W. O. Hirt 1987. Derechos: Widespread convectively induced windstorms. Wea. Forecasting. 2. 32–49.

description: Digital reference services that use the Internet to connect people with people who can answer questions about the Earth and geological sciences.
name: ASK-A GEOLOGIST

description: Fire applied in a knowledgeable manner to forest fuels on a specific land area under selected weather conditions to accomplish predetermined, well-defined management objectives.
name: PRESCRIBED BURNS/FIRES

description: A change imposed upon the climate system which modifies the radiative balance of that system. The causes of such a change may include changes in the sun, clouds, ice, greenhouse gases, volcanic activity, and other agents. Radiative forcing is often specified as the net change in energy flux at the troposphere (watts per square meter). Radiative forcing may sometimes be referred to as external forcing or perturbations of the climate.
name: RADIATIVE FORCING
reference: Mintzer, I.M., ed. Confronting Climate Change: Risks, Implications, and Responses, Cambridge University Press, Cambridge, UK. Maunder, W.J. 1994. Dictionary of Global Climate Change, 2nd ed. Chapman and Hall, NY

description: Consists of oxygenated compounds that are organic derivitives of hydrogen peroxide. These compounds are formed in the oxidation of hydrocarbons in relatively clean air, where oxides of nitrogen are not abundant.
name: HYDROPEROXY
reference: American Meteorological Society. 2000. Glossary of Meteorology, Second Edition. Boston, MA: American Meteorological Society.

description: Soil formed in either mineral or organic materials having permafrost either within 1 m below the surface or, if the soil is strongly cryoturbated, with 2 m below the surface, and having a mean annual ground temperature below 0 deg C.
name: CRYOSOLS
reference: National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC). "http://nsidc.org"

description: Describes a geomorphic process related to freezing of water occur. In its original meaning a periglacial area was at the time in question, the area was not buried by glacial ice but was subject to intense freezing cycles and exhibits permafrost weathering and erosion characteristics.
name: PERIGLACIAL PROCESSES

description: The difference in height between two levels in the glacier or ice sheet.
name: GLACIER/ICE SHEET THICKNESS

description: The Concentration of element Lead (Pb) in the atmosphere.
name: LEAD

description: The down slope movement of soil, rock, and other weathered materials because of gravity.
name: LANDSLIDE

description: The WP pattern is a primary mode of low-frequency variability over the North Pacific in all months, and has been previously described by both Barnston and Livezey (1987) and Wallace and Gutzler (1981). During winter and spring, the pattern consists of a north-south dipole of anomalies, with one center located over the Kamchatka Peninsula and another broad center of opposite sign covering portions of southeastern Asia and the low latitudes of the extreme western North Pacific. Therefore, strong positive or negative phases of this pattern reflect pronounced zonal and meridional variations in the location and intensity of the entrance region of the Pacific (or East Asian) jet steam. In the summer and fall, the WP pattern becomes increasingly wave-like, and a third prominent center appears over Alaska and the Beaufort Sea, with a sign opposite to the center over the western North Pacific. This wave structure is most evident in the Fall, when it extends downstream along a quasi great-circle route into the western United States. The time series of the WP pattern indicates considerable intermonthly and interannual variability, and persistence of a particular phase of the pattern is relatively common.
name: WEST PACIFIC INDEX
reference: Source: NOAA Climate Prediction Center, http://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/

description: A vertical representation of SF6- an inert gas categorized as hydrofluorocarbons. Sulfur hexafluoride absorbs thermal infrared radiation and could increase global warming as its concentration in the atmosphere increases; therefore it is a greenhouse gas.
name: SULFUR HEXAFLUORIDE PROFILES

description: The transport of a mass of sediment particles per unit area per unit time.
name: PARTICLE FLUX
reference: Adapted from: Neshyba, S. 1987. Oceanography, Perspectives on a Fluid Earth. John Wiley and Sons, Inc. p. 482.

description: Pertaining to the characteristics of the layer of ice crystals that forms between the ground and snow cover by sublimation. It's also referred to as sugar snow.
name: DEPTH HOAR
reference: Goudie, Andrew. 1997. The Encyclopedic Dictionary of Physical Geography. Blackwell Publishing, Malden, Massachusetts.

description: Pertaining to the environment of rock-dominated shorelines, often characterized by high-energy wave action, and often common along isostatically rebounding coastlines.
name: ROCKY COASTS

description: The effects of roll, pitch, and yaw, as well as jitter on the image geometry. Roll will cause the image to take on a wavy appearance, pitch will cause grid cells to contract or expand in the flight direction, and yaw will create a skewed image. Jitter consists of random and unsystematic vibaration which cannot be measured.

description: Spectral fraction of photometric shade.
name: SHADE FRACTION

description: Chemical component of the ocean used to determine the movement of water masses.
name: OCEAN TRACERS

description: Refers to the chemical composition of the surface water of rivers, lakes, streams, and reservoirs including water quality and contamination.
name: SURFACE WATER CHEMISTRY
reference: Goudie, Andrew. 1997. The Encyclopedic Dictionary of Physical Geography. Blackwell Publishing, Malden, Massachusetts.

description: A sudden and violent release of matter and energy within a solar activity region in the form of electromagnetic radiation, energetic particles, shock waves, lasting a few minutes to hours. Solar flares accelerate charged particles into interplanetary space.
name: SOLAR FLARES
reference: the Cambridge Encyclopedia of the Sun, The Cambridge University Press, Cambridge, CB2, 2RU, UK, 2001. (Excerpted)

description: Pertaining to the occurence, extent, and severity of whiteout conditions.
name: WHITEOUT

description: A service that aids in the classification of objects in an ordered system that indicates natural relationships. This may include taxonomy.
name: IDENTIFICATION/CLASSIFICATION SYSTEMS

description: A charged molecule composed of one atom of nitrogen and three atoms of oxygen, NO3-, available to plants and phytoplankton as a nutrient.
name: NITRATE

description: Survival is the converse of mortality for an organism. Survival is a result of a combination of factors that contribute toward successful reproductive advantage and the ability to resist being killed or eaten by another species.
name: SURVIVAL RATES
reference: Krebs, C. 1994. Ecology. HarperCollins. New York, New York and Hickman, C. and L. Roberts. 1995. Animal Diversity. William C. Brown Publishers. Dubuque, IA.

description: Erosional downcutting or downward erosion or vertical erosion is a geological process that deepens the channel of a stream or valley by removing material from the stream's bed or the valley's floor.
name: DOWNCUTTING

description: An area of land that is always soaked with water; low, wet land that supports grass and trees.
name: SWAMP
